title: Generating parquet file with bloom filter
question:
I am looking to partition raw parquet data in AWS S3 by YYYYMMDD and to enable bloom filters on high cardinality column (let's say QID).

import boto3
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import col, from_unixtime, substring, concat, expr

# Initialize Spark Session with Bloom Filter Support

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("Enable Bloom Filters in Parquet") \
    .config("spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.impl", "org.apache.hadoop.fs.s3a.S3AFileSystem") \
    .config("parquet.bloom.filter.enabled", "true") \
    .config("parquet.bloom.filter.column.names", "QID") \
    .config("parquet.bloom.filter.expected.ndv", "300000") \
    .config("parquet.writer.version", "v2") \
    .config("parquet.pushdown", "true") \
    .config("parquet.enable.dictionary", "false") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Load all Parquet files
df = spark.read.parquet(""s3://dev/source/") 

transformed_df = df.withColumn("TIM_YYYYMMDD", expr("FLOOR(TIM_LONG / 10000)").cast("long"))

transformed_df.coalesce(1).write \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .partitionBy("TIM_YYYYMMDD") \
    .parquet("s3://dev/target")

I have tested this with pyspark 3.5.5 (locally & also with AWS Glue ETL). All method generates the parquet files, but the parquet metadata does not show any presence of bloom filter applied on column QID

parquet-tools meta part-00000-009a5011-e87b-4896-b828-d716f2d25e2a.c000.snappy.parquet

I was expecting to see "BF" or "bloom Filter" keywords in the parquet metadata to provide the presence of bloom filters.

Can someone please advise what am i missing here?
answer:
Firstly, you tried to specify a column wise configuration for configuring a Parquet Bloom Filter. One can also opt to globally enable Bloom Filters for all columns. Therefore you must specify:

"parquet.bloom.filter.enabled", "true"

However, in your case you need to enable it for a specific column. This is done by specifying the column name within the property followed by #. So in your case, you set the Bloom Filter configuration for specific columns as follows:

"parquet.bloom.filter.enabled#QID", true
"parquet.bloom.filter.expected.ndv#QID", 300000

Where #<column_name> part indicates which column you want the bloom filter to be built on. Without that suffix, Parquet doesn’t know which column the option applies to and will create Bloom Filters for all columns.

Moreover, the configuration "parquet.bloom.filter.column.names" is not working. From what I can find in the Parquet Issues, it was part of an experimental proposal (over 5 years ago) but never implemented in the released Parquet spec.

Secondly, and this is why you the bloom filter is not created in the first place, is that you are creating these configurations on the session-level, not through the writer options, where they actually should be specified.

Your dataframewriter should be configured, instead of the spark session:

transformed_df.coalesce(1).write \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .option("parquet.bloom.filter.enabled#QID", "true")
    .option("parquet.bloom.filter.expected.ndv#QID", "300000")
    .partitionBy("TIM_YYYYMMDD") \
    .parquet("s3://dev/target")

Now you will have the file written as expected, with a Bloom filter structure in the column chunk metadata for column QID.
